content:
customer-alice: Hi — running into intermittent truncated streaming responses. Pattern: client aborts the stream and immediately reconnects; the resumed stream is missing the final tokens from the previous response ~20% of the time. Happening on JS SDK 2.3.0 in our browser app.

support_jen: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal repro + SDK version and any request IDs or headers you see?

customer-alice: SDK 2.3.0 (browser). Minimal repro is basically: abort + immediate reconnect. Example: 

```ts
// pseudo-repro
const ac = new AbortController();
fetch('/v1/stream', { method: 'POST', body: prompt, signal: ac.signal });
// abort then reconnect quickly
ac.abort();
setTimeout(() => fetch('/v1/stream', { method: 'POST', body: prompt }), 50);
```

Observed output: first stream finishes with "...over the lazy" and after reconnect we start with "dog" — the token "dog" should have been last token of previous stream, so the final bits get dropped on resume. No explicit resume token in our client.

ryan: Thanks — can you also share any stream headers (x-stream-seq, last-event-id) and the network logs? Does the client reuse the same session id or create a fresh one when it reconnects?

customer-alice: headers show x-stream-seq: 102 then after reconnect x-stream-seq: 103. We don't set a resume token; client reuses the same session cookie so it looks like a continuation.

samir: Reproduced locally with a small Node EventSource wrapper + AbortController. I see the same missing tail. Quick capture from server side logs: 

"[runtime] session=abc123 seq=102 finalize-scheduled"
"[runtime] session=abc123 connection=old closed by client (abort)"
"[runtime] session=abc123 connection=new handshake received, treating as continuation"
"[runtime] session=abc123 finalize completed but final buffer was not flushed to new connection"

Hypothesis: race between finalize/flush and new handshake. If the new handshake is accepted as continuation before finalize flush completes, the runtime can mark the final chunk as already delivered or drop the buffered tail — resulting in missing tokens.

ryan: That matches our instrumentation traces. Workarounds we can recommend now:
- add a short backoff before reconnecting (>=150ms) to allow finalize/flush to complete
- if possible, send a resume token/explicit sequence id so the runtime can reconcile
- avoid reusing the exact same session id immediately after abort (create a new session id)

eng-qa: Triage: created INF-8231. Root cause: session state machine allows handshakes to be marked as continuation while finalize is still in-flight. Fix plan: make finalize atomic or ensure new handshake waits for finalize/force-flush buffer to new connection.

dev-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5542 — runtime: flush-finalize-wait. CI: canary build 2.3.2-beta.1 created.

samir: Deployed canary to staging. @customer-alice if you can test 2.3.2-beta.1 or use the canary runtime, please try your repro (we added an explicit finalize wait + extra logging).

customer-alice: Will try now with browser SDK pointed at canary. Quick test looks promising — retried abort/reconnect loop 50x with no missing tokens so far.

support_jen: For tracking: assigned INF-8231 to eng-runtime, target delivery v2.4.7, public SDK/stable patch planned after canary validation.

customer-alice: Beta fixed it for us — no truncation on repeated abort/reconnect. Thanks for the quick turnaround! :100: 

ryan: Great news. We'll promote the patch to stable and include the fix in release notes. In the meantime, recommend customers use the small reconnect backoff or the canary if they hit this in prod.

eng-qa: Postmortem note: add unit tests for overlapping handshake/finalize race and add e2e abort/reconnect stress test to CI.

support_jen: Closing loop here — please ping if anything else shows up, and we'll update the incident INF-8231 timeline.
